html:
SMTO-LLM-0073 — The model server sent a reply SMTO couldn't use

GUID: 66bee9d4-93dd-52a6-8c20-b6ffd07a6087
Slug: local-ai-endpoint-incompatible
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO got a reply from the model server or the Gateway, but it was too large, incomplete or in a form SMTO doesn't understand. SMTO didn't treat it as a success.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, open the Local AI Runtime profile you used, and confirm its provider (for example Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp) and port match the server running there. If the profile points at a different kind of program, its replies won't be in the form SMTO expects.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. If that Gateway shows Update available, ask the person who manages it to update it. A Gateway and SMTO on different versions can disagree about what a reply should contain.
  3. If you were starting a server or downloading or removing a model, ask SMTO to list the model servers and installed models on that Gateway before you try again. The error alone does not establish whether that change already happened on the Gateway computer.

What success looks like

  • Asking SMTO for that model server's models returns a normal list of model names.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this may need a fix in SMTO or in the model server. Don't repeat a start, download or removal until you've checked what's already there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Local AI response failed validation: the provider's model list or metadata was malformed or over 256 KiB, the Gateway's receipt had the wrong shape, or (during activation) the controller's /models probe failed or returned a non-200 status.

What this means

  • Model inventory or Gateway response validation rejected the response shape, bounds or required receipt fields; the category covers more than a model-list mismatch. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • Model inventory or Gateway response validation rejected the response shape, bounds or required receipt fields; the category covers more than a model-list mismatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the failed boundary was inventory discovery or Gateway receipt validation; compare required fields and size limits at that boundary.

How to fix it

  • Query the profile endpoint's models path directly and confirm it returns OpenAI-style JSON with a data list of 1-1024 string ids under 256 KiB, and that the provider type in the profile matches the actual server. If the Gateway receipt was rejected, update the Gateway and Server to matching versions; for a write (start, pull, remove), inspect runtimes and installed models before repeating it.
  • Repair the responding provider/Gateway compatibility issue and reconcile any mutation separately before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The same operation returns a bounded response satisfying its inventory or receipt contract.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
